title: Theory: async/await
code:
import asyncio


async def download(url):
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    return url


async def main(urls):
    results = []
    #!teoria async/await
    for url in urls:
        results.append(await download(url))
    return results
fix_lines: results = await asyncio.gather(*(download(url) for url in urls))
rubric: Deep shape: what it is, why, how it really works (coroutine objects, the event loop scheduling them, what `await` suspends), a minimal example, that the loop at line 12 awaits one download at a time (in words), and pointers to read next.
